summary: A suggestion for NETBANK, a single billing and account creation system for the network. A project manager would authorize users and set up accounts across many hosts, receiving one combined bill. The manager would go through introductions and funding checks only once.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 408 proposes one account and billing arrangement for users working across network hosts. A project manager would authorize users once and receive one bill for the accounts they used.

questions: how does netbank simplify arpanet access
what problem did netbank aim to solve
how would netbank manage user accounts
how would netbank combine network charges
subtitle: A proposed single system for network accounts and billing

tldr.problem: A project manager might have to arrange access and funding separately for users at different server hosts.
tldr.mechanism: NETBANK would let a manager authorize users and create accounts for all or selected server hosts through one initialization process.
tldr.outcome: Usage across those accounts would be combined into one bill for the project manager.

today: RFC 408 proposes a centralized account and billing service called NETBANK. It describes the intended model, not an implemented service.

sections.title: One Setup for a Project
sections.content: The RFC proposes a single billing and account creation system for a goal-oriented project. The project manager would introduce themselves and verify funding once, rather than repeat that initialization for each server host.
sections.plainLanguage: A project manager would complete the introduction and funding check once. The proposal aims to avoid repeating that process at every host.

sections.title: Authorizing Users Across Hosts
sections.content: The manager would authorize a set of user IDs to use resources across the whole network or a specified subset of server hosts. The proposal also provides accounts for users to spend while using those resources, with the charges included in one bill to the manager.
sections.plainLanguage: The manager would choose which users could access which hosts. Their account charges would be collected for one bill.

sections.title: A Login Check at the Host
sections.content:
NETBANK would require a login option that tells a server to check the NETBANK facility on the system hosting it. The author says this could support controlled, funded experimentation by project members and encourage server hosts to offer resources that might begin with low usage.

The RFC presents this as an idea for a protocol or service.
sections.plainLanguage: When a user logged in, the host would check NETBANK for the project's authorization. The document proposes this service but does not describe a completed system.
